subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both paths change a sensitive provider credential boundary, and automation should not decide whether node hosts may acquire and transfer gateway-owned OAuth material without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC or setup flow that moves provider auth material into the gateway store without consuming tokens into the node-local store first.

options.title: Warn but keep permissive
options.body: Warn node-host users that auth only affects the local node, accepting the wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction while preserving local loopback and tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: They already authored and verified the maintainer repair direction for the exact remote-node auth guard.
